s.how: Bring 150g each of aged cheddar, brie and blue cheese to room temperature. Arrange on a wooden board with oatcakes, a slab of quince paste, sliced apple and a handful of walnuts. Set it by the fire with a glass of something warm.

s.note: Amanda and Graham at the local pub
s.how: Mix 500g pork mince with a grated onion, chopped sage and salt. Lay along 2 halved puff pastry sheets, roll up and seal. Brush with beaten egg, cut into bites and bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve warm with English mustard.

m.note: dinner with Graham and his two daughters
m.how: Simmer 2 cans crushed tomatoes with 80g butter and a peeled halved onion for 45 minutes, stirring now and then. Remove the onion and season. Toss with 500g cooked spaghetti, then finish with torn basil and plenty of grated parmesan.

w.how: Soak 200g chopped dates in 250ml boiling water with a pinch of bicarb. Cream 60g butter with 150g brown sugar, add 2 eggs, the dates and 175g self-raising flour. Bake at 180C for 35 minutes, poke holes and pour over hot toffee sauce. Serve with ice cream.

d.note: Christmas by the fire in the cottage
d.how: Pour a bottle of red wine into a pot with a sliced orange, 2 cinnamon sticks, 4 whole cloves, a star anise and 2 tbsp honey. Warm gently for 20 minutes, never letting it boil. Ladle into mugs by the fire with snow falling outside.
